absent: Numeric values and types of port mask and offset and their platform variability.
Concurrency and locking rules for managed allocation, add, release and match beyond the fragments shown.
Full selection and update semantics for dynamic debug queries, iterators and flag masks.
Error values and side effects of architecture memory-type reservation primitives.
Key selection behaviour when keyring lookup finds multiple candidates or a revoked key.
Exact throughput computation and rounding for very large iteration counts and timer granularity.
Conditions selecting each build identifier format alternative.

findings.text: Device-managed port mapping binds a port range mapping to a device lifetime. Mapping takes a device plus port and count and returns an opaque handle or a null failure. Unmapping releases the entry tied to a supplied handle. Dedicated release and match helpers identify the stored handle for teardown.
Raw port mapping converts a port number and length into an opaque address handle with range rejection, while raw unmapping accepts such a handle and has no observable effect in this configuration.

Device-managed architecture memory-type helpers attach write-combining reservations to a device. One adds a physical range and reports a small token or negative error. Another reserves a typed range described by start and length and reports status. Companion release helpers undo each reservation on managed free.

Synthetic benchmark entry runs a fixed workload for a requested iteration count and reports throughput. It allocates linked record state, initializes globals and arrays, executes a defined procedure mix, logs validation of final values, frees allocations, and returns a rate or a negative error.

Signature verification checks supplied data against a binary signature using a user key selected by an identifier carried in the signature header. It hashes data plus header, verifies the trailing signature bytes with RSA, and returns success or a negative error for malformed input, unsupported algorithm, missing key, or mismatch.

Formatting and dump helpers provide a string formatter returning a count, an early-boot arch description setter that records formatted text in a fixed buffer, and a register-report entry that forwards a log level to the common dump information printer.
Managed reservation record for typed ranges holds a start and a size in resource-sized unsigned values, enough to release exactly the reserved interval later.

Benchmark record links to another record, carries a discriminator selecting one of three variant payloads, and stores enumeration, integer, character and short string members. Supporting aliases define bounded integers, characters, fixed-length strings, and fifty-element one- and two-dimensional integer arrays, with pointer and value forms of the record.

Dynamic debug control separates per-module tables, selection queries, iteration cursors, flag updates, and a flag text buffer. Tables link modules and map ranges to descriptor arrays with counts. Queries filter by file, module, function, format, class string and line interval. Cursors pair a table with an index. Updates carry desired bits plus mask. The text buffer is sized to the flag option count.

RSA verification holds the target key read semaphore across payload access, header checks and public-key extraction, releasing on every exit including revoked-key, short-payload and parse-failure paths.
Dynamic debug configuration defines a dedicated mutex alongside its control structures, indicating exclusive update discipline for table and flag changes.
Port mapping rejects ports above a platform mask and otherwise derives the handle by adding a platform offset to the port number, so valid handles form a shifted contiguous range.

Device-managed helpers follow allocate-then-commit discipline: allocate a small node, attempt the underlying operation, attach the node to the device on success, and discard the node without attaching on failure. Allocation failure yields null or memory-exhaustion status with no attachment.

Benchmark result is a non-negative rate derived from iteration count and elapsed milliseconds and requires a minimum two-second measurement window. Shorter runs report a retry signal, allocation failures report memory exhaustion, and final globals and record fields are expected to equal documented constants checked by logging helpers.

RSA path enforces layered validation: payload length and header version, algorithm and component count, successful parsing of both key parts, non-zero modulus length, bounded result size, padding separation with minimum-length and separator rules, and exact match of decoded digest length and content to the computed hash.

String formatting delegates to a bounded variant with a very large limit and returns its count. Arch description formatting is bounded to its destination buffer. Build identifier display has two compile-time alternatives, one emitting a fixed-width hash field from the build identifier and one emitting an empty marker.

Debug flag options map one-to-one to output controls for enable, module name, function name, source name, line number, thread identity, stack detail, and clear, with an internal verbosity level and a path-prefix trimming rule that falls back to no trimming on mismatch.

Benchmark driver has explicit-count and auto-scale modes. Explicit mode runs once with the configured count. Auto-scale starts from a reference value and doubles until the run stops reporting too-short timing or the doubling sequence ends, then reports throughput and derived units, a retry hint, or a failure.
Port unmap follows warn-on-unmatched discipline: lookup by handle equality drives release, and absence of a matching managed entry triggers a warning rather than silent success.

Parameter and init entries gate benchmark execution on a boolean flag and running system state. Parameter writes update the flag and may trigger an immediate run, while init performs a single boot-time run when the flag was preset.

Unmapping with an unknown handle warns instead of succeeding silently, so callers cannot assume idempotence. Mapping failure is signaled by null and must be checked before use. Managed node allocation can fail under memory pressure.

Signature parsing consumes identifier and key material from untrusted buffers under explicit length checks, and every failure path must release partial key components, temporary buffers and key references to avoid leaks or use after revocation.
Reference throughput constant used as auto-scale start and derived-unit divisor has value 1757.
Benchmark enumeration defines five ordered values, string payloads use thirty-one byte arrays, and integer array dimensions are fixed at fifty in each dimension.
